nodes.name: Hydrothermal Ni(OH)₂ growth
nodes.procedure: Ni(OH)₂ microsheet arrays were grown on Ni foam via a hydrothermal method.
nodes.source_text: First, Ni(OH)₂ microsheet arrays were grown on Ni foam via a hydrothermal method...

nodes.name: Bimetal co-modification hydrothermal
nodes.procedure: CoFe-Ni(OH)₂ microsheet arrays were obtained via a second hydrothermal process in an aqueous solution containing Fe³⁺ and Co²⁺, which leads to nanostructural transformation from smooth microsheet to hierarchically nanosheet-assembled-microsheet structure after a dissolution-reconstruction process. That is, nickel hydroxides were etched by H⁺ ions from the hydrolytic reaction of Fe³⁺, resulting in partial dissolution and release of Ni species. Then Fe³⁺ and Co²⁺ ions gradually diffused into Ni(OH)₂ microsheets and subsequently co-precipitated with Ni species and OH⁻ to generate the hierarchical nanostructure.
nodes.source_text: Second, Co and Fe co-modified Ni(OH)₂ [denoted as CoFe-Ni(OH)₂] microsheet arrays were obtained via a second hydrothermal process in an aqueous solution containing Fe³⁺ and Co²⁺...

nodes.name: Phosphating conversion
nodes.procedure: These pure and metal-modified Ni(OH)₂ precursors were converted to corresponding metal phosphides (Ni₂P, Fe-Ni₂P, Co-Ni₂P, and CoFe-Ni₂P, respectively) via phosphating process.
nodes.source_text: Finally, these pure and metal-modified Ni(OH)₂ precursors were converted to corresponding metal phosphides... via phosphating process.

nodes.name: Ni-felt electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: The CoFe-Ni₂P catalyst was grown on a Ni felt (CoFe-Ni₂P/Ni-felt) as both anode and cathode.
nodes.source_text: a flow-type AEM electrolyzer single cell was assembled, in which the CoFe-Ni₂P catalyst was grown on a Ni felt (CoFe-Ni₂P/Ni-felt) as both anode and cathode

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows uniform smooth microsheet morphology for Ni(OH)₂ and hierarchical nanosheet-assembled microsheet structure for CoFe-Ni(OH)₂ after dissolution-reconstruction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the uniform and smooth microsheet morphology were revealed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Figure 1b)... leads to nanostructural transformation from smooth microsheet to hierarchically nanosheet-assembled-microsheet structure (Figure 1c)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern of Ni₂P shows diffraction peaks at 40.66°, 47.27°, and 54.07° corresponding to (111), (210), and (002) planes; metal-modified Ni₂P shows peak shift for (111) plane with no impurities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern of the Ni₂P electrode in Figure 1e exhibits three diffraction peaks at about 40.66°, 47.27°, and 54.07°, which correspond to (111), (210), and (002) planes of Ni₂P... obvious shift for the (111) plane

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM of CoFe-Ni₂P shows lattice fringes of 0.256, 0.253, and 0.191 nm assigned to (101), (200), and (210) planes of Ni₂P with many crystalline-amorphous phase interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) image of CoFe-Ni₂P shown in Figure 1f, the lattice fringes with interplanar spacing of 0.256, 0.253, and 0.191 nm were assigned to the (101), (200), and (210) planes of Ni₂P

nodes.characterization_summary: Dark-field TEM image with corresponding EDX elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Ni, Co, Fe, P in CoFe-Ni₂P; EDX spectrum gives atomic ratio Ni:Fe:Co:P ≈ 1.00:0.28:0.12:0.86.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) mapping images verify the uniform distribution of Ni, Co, Fe, and P elements in the CoFe-Ni₂P microsheets (Figure 1g), and the corresponding EDX spectrum shows that the atomic ratio of Ni:Fe:Co:P is about 1.00:0.28:0.12:0.86

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS shows for Ni₂P: Ni 2p Ni-P peaks at ≈853.1, 870.3 eV and Ni-POx at ≈856.86, 874.80 eV; P 2p M-P at 129.85 eV, P-O at 134.13 eV. CoFe-Ni₂P shows positive shifts indicating electron transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: there are two characteristic peaks of Ni-P species at ≈853.1 and 870.3 eV, as well as a pair of peaks at ≈856.86 and 874.80 eV from oxidized Ni-P species (Ni-POx)... The high-resolution P 2p spectra... including metal-P (M-P) bonds at 129.85 eV and oxidized P (P-O) bonds at 134.13 eV

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Ni K-edge XANES shows higher absorption edge for CoFe-Ni₂P than Ni₂P, indicating higher Ni oxidation state after bimetal modification.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the normalized X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of Ni K-edge in Figure 2e shown, both the Ni₂P and CoFe-Ni₂P catalysts display higher absorption edge position than that of Ni foil... higher Ni oxidation state of the CoFe-Ni₂P catalyst than the Ni₂P catalyst

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ni-P1 at ≈2.24 Å, Ni-P2 at 2.54 Å, Ni-Ni at ≈2.57 Å for Ni₂P; CoFe-Ni₂P shows slightly shorter Ni-P2 and Ni-Ni paths with decreased coordination number.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2f exhibits Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra... After Co and Fe co-modification, the Ni-P1 path of CoFe-Ni₂P remains almost unchanged, while the Ni-P2 and Ni-Ni paths become slightly shorter

nodes.characterization_summary: Cdl calculated from CV at non-Faradaic potentials: CoFe-Ni₂P = 8.66 mF/cm², Fe-Ni₂P = 6.82 mF/cm², Ni₂P = 1.37 mF/cm² indicating increased ECSA by metal modification.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Double-layer capacitance (Cdl) was calculated from cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves to estimate the electrochemically active surface area (ECSA)... CoFe-Ni₂P (8.66 mFcm⁻²) and Fe-Ni₂P (6.82 mFcm⁻²) electrodes, which are almost six and five times that of pure Ni₂P (1.37 mFcm⁻²)

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows smallest Rct of ≈1.52 Ω for CoFe-Ni₂P at 285 mV overpotential.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As the electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) shows in Figure 3e... a smallest Rct of ≈1.52 Ω is achieved by the CoFe-Ni₂P electrode

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-OER Raman shows peaks at ≈474 and 554 cm⁻¹ ascribed to δ(Ni-O) and ν(Ni-O) of NiOOH; in situ Raman shows reconstruction to CoFe-NiOOH at lower potentials.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Meanwhile, the Raman spectra of the CoFe-Ni₂P electrode... exhibit two characteristic peaks at ≈474 and 554 cm⁻¹, which are ascribed to δ(Ni-O) and ν(Ni-O) vibration modes of NiOOH

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS detects significant P leaching after CV activation and during 18h OER at 100 mA/cm², with slow increase of Ni, Co, Fe concentrations indicating good stability.
nodes.evidence_snippet: inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) was carried out to determine element contents in electrolyte... After CV activation, a large amount of P was detected... For the three metal elements, their concentrations in the electrolyte increased slowly

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern of CoFe-Ni₂P shows diffraction rings of (200), (111), (210), (002) planes of Ni₂P, consistent with XRD.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of CoFe-Ni₂P illustrates the diffraction patterns of (200), (111), (210), and (002) planes of Ni₂P (Figure S11)
